checks: Linear interpolation has slopes equal to the nondecreasing outward drops in reverse order on the left, then zero, then their negatives in forward order. The resulting concave nonnegative radius subgraph is compact and convex, has interior over (0,1), and has exactly the integer fibers −m through m+1. Terminal zero radii produce points of zero d-volume and no fibers are omitted.

Tightening a containing halfspace to y can only decrease its mass. A base-only halfspace retains at least one entire fiber of each reflected pair, including any boundary fibers. For a nonzero continuous normal with a negative entry, the swap of a minimum coordinate with the slack is an affine involution on each positive-radius simplex and preserves its volume. The transformed coefficients are w_i=−v_i>0 and w_j=v_j−v_i≥0. The new ambient margin minus the transformed margin is (R−r)v_i≤0, so the new cap is contained fiber by fiber and passes through the same y.

After division by the positive continuous coefficient sum, the paired +β tilt minus the paired −β tilt is exactly the sum of two nonnegative differences of the nonincreasing F_r. The smaller −β tilt at bases −h and h+1 has thresholds t−βh and t+β(h+1). This sign and both integer labels agree with all subsequent invocations.

The planar theorem handles all d=2. For d=1 the only normalized normal is u_1=1=2/(d+1), covered by the large-coordinate theorem. For d≥3 that theorem also handles equality at the cutoff. In the remaining sector m=0 is covered by the own left centroid cap; for m≥1 the affine replacement compares actual cap mass minus target mass term by term, for each chain’s own mass, while retaining the very same cap, centroid, and actual finite bases.

Scaling x by 1/R divides the tilt and radius slope by R, with a common volume factor R^d. The easy range β≥at gives t−βh≤tr_h on each positive-radius simplex. This includes a=0 and equality; every left cap there contains its own centroid and already supplies its pair’s target mass.

In the hard range a>0 and 0≤β<at the two normalized threshold derivatives have strictly positive numerators at−β and β+a(t+β). By homogeneity the paired fraction per r_h^d is nonincreasing. A negative sum of positive-weight deficits forces the last positive-radius fraction below Γ_d; all appended positive-radius terms then have negative deficit. The extension to h<1/a is finite and all ignored zero-radius terms have zero mass.

For r/(d+1)≤s<r/d, the point (s,…,s) lies on the cap boundary and has barycentrics s/r repeated d times and 1−ds/r, the last no larger than the others. All are at most 1/d, and omitting one of the largest in the exact product depth gives E_d(s,r) after multiplying by r^d. The claimed zero lower bound for s≥r/d is automatic. Both actual thresholds satisfy s≥tr>0 on the positive full leg.

At h=0 the left envelope is E_d(t,1)=Γ_d. The reviewed angular bound adds more than Γ_d/6 to that one term only. The accepted full-leg theorem bounds target minus the sum of both envelopes strictly below Γ_d/6, yielding a positive actual surplus and ruling out a negative original prefix. The signs of the draft’s cap-minus-target surplus and the predecessor’s target-minus-envelope deficit are used consistently.

For m=0 any mixed point lies in one of the two equal positive simplices. Choose a barycentric coordinate λ_i≥1/(d+1); the closed vertex-side cap λ_i(x)≥λ_i has fraction (1−λ_i)^d≤Γ_d, including a vertex itself. Add a finite multiple of the base displacement from that point’s base with sign negative at the other base. Compactness lets it exclude the other fiber while leaving the chosen cap unchanged. This gives depth at most Γ_d/2 everywhere and equality at y by the lower bound.
